hint_text: SHOPPING LIST: 1 NOT chip, 1 AND chip, 2 OR chips, 1 display, 1 DIP switch, 3 big resistors (10k), 7 small resistors (220), 1 breadboard with jumper wires, 1 power supply. That is 18 pieces.
Heavy stuff stays in the tall metal cabinet with two doors on the back wall: the bench power supply is in there.
Logic chips are like trash to this office: look in the recycling bins in the bottom-left corner (green and yellow).
Resistors with BIG values (10k) hide in things people drink from, write with or listen with: a bottle, a pen cup, a headset.
Seven small 220 ohm resistors sit in office binders: two on the top-row desks, two in the middle row, one at the bottom-left desk and two on the bookshelf on the right.
OR chips like plants: one by the water cooler on the left wall and one behind the pink beanbag. Breadboards and wires: a box on the shelf rack under the projector.
Boss: 'The display? We keep spare parts in the cardboard box on the floor next to my desk. And that little blue box on top of the gray cabinet is a DIP switch.'
Hidden things have no marker: walk close to anything suspicious and press Space to search it. Notes, screens and boards around the office hold hints. Hints you read are saved in the notebook (N).
When the Parts counter reaches 18/18, come to the bottom-right desk. The decoder bench is right here.
intro: Welcome to the lab, intern! I am your Boss.
Today's job: build a 7-segment decoder on the bench. It must show the characters C, P, E, -, 3 and 9.
First, collect the 18 parts hidden around the office. Walk close to anything suspicious and press Space to search it. Notes, screens and boards hold hints.
You are wearing the workshop shirt you earned in the last stage. It has a skill: for 10 seconds you can SEE the hidden parts. Watch, I will show you once!
See them glowing? Work for 2 minutes and you can use the skill one more time, whenever you like. A SKILL button lights up at the top right (key E, or flip SW13).

When you have everything, go to the decoder bench at the bottom-right desk and wire the breadboard: give every chip +5V and GND, power the DIP switch, add the pull-down and display resistors. The switches SW2-SW0 let you test your circuit.
Finished? Bring it to me. I will test it and tell you if it is right or wrong. A wrong answer costs a heart!
I will be at my desk on the right. Good luck!

BOOST: Saved for the Obby stage. No effect here.
ARMOR: Blocks the next failed QA penalty.
FREEZE: Stops moving obstacles for 5 s. Saved for Stage 3.
